item.title: Use the repo's money rounding helper for any monetary result
item.description: Monetary values must be rounded with the project's round_money (half-up to the cent), not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
item.content: Before returning any computed money value, check ledgerly/money.py for helpers like round_money and to_money and wrap the result. Banker's rounding silently produces wrong invoice totals that hidden tests will catch.

item.title: Read existing sibling functions to infer conventions
item.description: Existing functions in the same module (line_total, invoice_total) reveal the expected patterns for rounding, coercion, and zero handling.
item.content: When adding a new function, inspect neighboring implementations first: they show which helpers to import (ZERO, round_money, to_money) and how edge cases like empty collections are handled.

item.title: Handle empty-collection edge cases explicitly
item.description: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero.
item.content: Compute the denominator first and short-circuit with the canonical zero value (ZERO) rather than relying on exceptions or returning a plain 0, keeping types consistent with the rest of the module.

item.title: Mirror existing error conventions before implementing
item.description: Grep the codebase for similar validation patterns and reuse the same error codes and message formats.
item.content: Before writing validation logic, search for existing BillingError usages (e.g. 'invalid_state', 'negative_amount') and copy their exact codes and message shapes. This keeps new code consistent with hidden-test expectations and existing modules.

item.title: Reject bools explicitly when validating integers
item.description: In Python, isinstance(True, int) is True, so guard against bool before int checks for quantity-like fields.
item.content: When a parameter must be a positive integer, check `isinstance(x, bool)` first and reject it, then check `isinstance(x, int)` and the range. Hidden tests often pass True/False to catch naive int validation.

item.title: Normalize money inputs through the project's helper
item.description: Convert unit_price via the existing to_money/round_money helper rather than trusting raw input types.
item.content: Pass user-supplied prices through the project's money conversion helper (e.g. to_money) before comparing to ZERO or storing, so strings, floats, and Decimals are handled uniformly and invalid values raise consistently.

item.title: Mirror existing sibling implementations for consistency
item.description: When adding a new function, look for a closely related existing function in the codebase and reuse its patterns.
item.content: Before implementing, grep for similar functions (e.g., current_period) and copy their structure: timezone normalization via ensure_utc, timedelta arithmetic, and floor-division period indexing. This keeps behavior consistent and avoids subtle bugs.

item.title: Handle boundary cases explicitly in periodic calculations
item.description: For 'first X strictly after Y' with periodic events, handle Y before start and Y exactly on a boundary.
item.content: Use `if after < start: return start + length` for pre-start inputs, and `n = (after - start) // length + 1` so that an `after` exactly on a renewal boundary returns the next one (strictly after). This satisfies the 'start itself is not a renewal' and 'strictly after' requirements.

item.title: Normalize datetimes through the project's helper
item.description: Use the project's ensure_utc (or equivalent) on all datetime inputs rather than ad-hoc tzinfo checks.
item.content: Calling ensure_utc on both `after` and `sub.started_at` enforces naive-datetime rejection and UTC conversion consistently with the rest of the codebase, preventing comparison errors between aware and naive datetimes.

item.title: Read team conventions from review comments before coding
item.description: The first attempt was rejected because it missed two team conventions (idempotency_key and approved_by) that were stated in review comments, not in the issue text.
item.content: When a task has review comments or a prior rejected attempt, treat every comment as a hard requirement even if the issue description doesn't mention it. Conventions like keyword-only idempotency keys and approval thresholds are often introduced after incidents and are enforced by hidden tests.

item.title: Search the repo for existing audit/idempotency patterns
item.description: The accepted solution reused ledgerly.audit.events() and audit.record() with an idempotency_key field rather than inventing a new mechanism.
item.content: Before implementing money-moving operations, grep for audit, idempotency, and approval in the codebase. Reuse the existing audit module's events()/record() API and include the idempotency_key in the recorded entry so retries can be detected.

item.title: Validate state, amount, and approval before mutating
item.description: The accepted refund checks status == 'captured', positive rounded amount, approval threshold, and cumulative refund cap before updating refunded_amount and status.
item.content: Order guards as: idempotency short-circuit, state check, amount normalization with round_money, approval check, then cumulative cap (refunded + amount <= captured). Only mutate payment.refunded_amount and set status to 'refunded' when the total reaches the captured amount, then record the audit entry and return the payment.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers for Decimal-safe arithmetic
item.description: When adding a pricing/money function to a codebase that already has to_money/round_money helpers, build on them instead of raw Decimal/float math.
item.content: Inspect sibling modules (money.py, invoice.py) for established conversion and rounding helpers before implementing. Using to_money/round_money keeps rounding policy consistent and avoids float pitfalls; the first attempt was accepted because it followed this pattern.

item.title: Validate numeric inputs with the project's error type and code convention
item.description: Range/format validation should raise the library's BillingError with a snake_case code, matching existing call sites.
item.content: Grep for BillingError usages to learn the code-string convention (e.g. 'invalid_state', 'non_positive_amount'). Raise BillingError('invalid_tax_rate', ...) for out-of-range or non-finite rates rather than ValueError, so callers can catch a single exception type.

item.title: Test edge cases manually before submitting
item.description: Run a quick script exercising boundary values (0, 100, invalid rates, string inputs) to catch issues hidden tests may probe.
item.content: After implementing, manually call the function with boundary and type-varied inputs (Decimal, str, int, out-of-range) and print results. This surfaced a float-input rejection in the transcript and confirms behavior beyond the single visible test.

item.title: Check repo conventions before implementing money operations
item.description: The first attempt failed because it missed a team convention (keyword-only idempotency_key on money-moving operations) that wasn't in the issue text.
item.content: Before implementing any payment/credit operation, scan README, CHANGELOG, and existing audit/operation code for cross-cutting conventions like idempotency keys, audit fields, or state guards. Hidden tests often enforce conventions not stated in the issue.

item.title: Apply idempotency consistently across related operations
item.description: The accepted fix added idempotency_key to both capture and the existing authorize, with a shared _already_applied helper checking audit.events().
item.content: When adding an idempotency convention, factor a helper that scans audit.events() for a matching key and returns early (returning the existing object or None) before mutating state. Include idempotency_key in every audit.record call and retrofit sibling operations like authorize for consistency.

item.title: Validate state before mutating and normalize timestamps
item.description: The accepted capture checks status == 'authorized', raises BillingError('invalid_state', ...), and calls ensure_utc(at) before storing captured_at.
item.content: For state-transition operations, guard the precondition first with a typed BillingError carrying a code and message, then normalize any datetime via ensure_utc before persisting, and record an audit event with the relevant fields.
